artifacts.summary: cs5_fs: sorry-free Hilbert derivation of FS := (<>A -> []B) -> [](A -> B) against CS5ModalAxiom. Footprint [propext, Classical.choice].

verification.scope_note: Probe verified standalone via `lake env lean` (outside the lake build tree). Cslib/ untouched, so mainline CI status is exactly Phase 18's green state.

memory_candidates: CSLib CS5: bBox (phi -> []<>phi) and bDia (<>[]phi -> phi), with kBox/kDia-derived monotonicity, form an ADJUNCTION <> -| []. This is the most useful structural fact about CS5: <> is a left adjoint (preserves all joins, so k3/k5 come free), [] a right adjoint, Fix(<>) = Fix([]).

CS5 algebraically = Heyting algebra H + complete sublattice J, <> the reflector and [] the coreflector onto J. kBox is then automatic; kDia is EQUIVALENT to Frobenius: <>(u /\ x) = u /\ <>x for u in J. This characterization decides FS-style questions fast and shows no CS5 countermodel to FS can exist.

Hilbert-system anti-pattern: concluding a formula is underivable because necessitation needs an empty context and 'the hypothesis must live in the context'. With the B axiom (phi -> []<>phi), internalize the hypothesis C as <>C instead: prove the CLOSED theorem |- <>C -> psi, necessitate that, apply k to get []<>C -> []psi, then bBox gives C -> []psi. This refuted a landed 'structural mismatch' obstruction claim in task 517.

FS1 (<>(A->B) -> ([]A -> <>B)) is derivable in PLAIN CK -- it is not the hard Fischer-Servi axiom. The hard one is FS2 = (<>A -> []B) -> [](A -> B) (Simpson's k4); CSLib's `FS` denotes FS2. Relevant when reading IK = CK + k3 + k4 + k5 against CK + FS1 + FS2.
